statusPolicy.note: Example items start in Inbox. Suggested statuses demonstrate triage possibilities and are not established workflow facts.

items.title: Require authentication for private file downloads
items.finding: Private files are served through a route that does not enforce an authenticated session.
items.description: Move private files behind an authenticated download handler, authorize access to the requested record, and remove direct public paths.
research: The current route resolves a file before checking the request identity.
validation: Verify anonymous requests receive 401.
Verify authorized users can download only files they are allowed to access.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example security finding.

items.title: Normalize uploaded filenames before writing to storage
items.finding: Client filenames are combined with a storage directory without normalization.
items.description: Discard client path segments, allow only expected extensions, generate unique server-side names, and verify the resolved path remains inside the upload directory.
research: Traversal and same-name collisions are possible when the original filename is trusted.
validation: Test traversal, absolute paths, separators, and invalid extensions.
Test simultaneous uploads that share an original filename.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example security finding.

items.title: Enforce administrator access on management endpoints
items.finding: The management page is hidden from ordinary users, but its API endpoints do not repeat the authorization check.
items.description: Apply the administrator policy to every management read and mutation at the server boundary.
research: Client-side navigation restrictions do not protect directly callable endpoints.
validation: Test administrator, ordinary authenticated, and anonymous requests.
Verify denied mutations do not change persisted data.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example security finding.

items.title: Protect account invitation actions from cross-site requests
items.finding: The invitation endpoint changes state without a cross-site request protection check.
items.description: Require POST, validate the request token, and keep recipient and role authorization on the server.
research: A signed-in browser could submit the action from an unrelated origin.
validation: Reject GET and missing or invalid request tokens.
Verify valid administrator invitations still succeed.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example security finding.

items.title: Restrict document deletion to owners and administrators
items.finding: The delete route accepts a document identifier without checking ownership.
items.description: Resolve the document server-side and require either ownership or the administrator role before deleting its stored object and database record.
research: The exact sharing rules should be confirmed before implementation.
validation: Attempt deletion as an unrelated user.
Verify owners and administrators can delete and an audit event is recorded.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example security finding.

items.title: Use explicit methods and request tokens for admin mutations
items.finding: Several administrative mutations accept multiple HTTP methods and omit request-token validation.
items.description: Limit state changes to POST or DELETE as appropriate, validate request tokens, and update existing clients without changing response contracts.
research: The routes are already grouped in one administrative router.
validation: Reject unsupported methods and missing tokens.
Run existing client tests for each migrated mutation.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example security finding.

items.title: Audit state-changing endpoints for authorization gaps
items.finding: Authorization and request-token handling vary across mutation endpoints.
items.description: Inventory state-changing routes, document their intended access policy, and create focused fixes only where server-side enforcement is missing.
research: Begin with account, document, and administrative routes.
validation: Record every mutation and its effective authorization policy.
Add negative tests for each confirmed gap.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example parent finding.

items.title: Redact sensitive fields from production logs
items.finding: Debug logging can include access tokens and complete request payloads.
items.description: Disable sensitive debug fields outside development and redact credentials, tokens, and personal fields in structured logs.
research: The production logging configuration inherits verbose request enrichment.
validation: Inspect production-mode logs for known sensitive field names.
Verify correlation and error context remain available.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example blocked finding.

items.title: Scan release artifacts for embedded secrets
items.finding: The release bundle is published without an automated secret scan.
items.description: Add a release-stage scan for credentials, private keys, environment files, and source maps containing configuration values.
research: The artifact layout must be confirmed with the delivery pipeline owner.
validation: Seed a harmless test marker and verify the scan blocks publication.
Confirm normal release artifacts pass.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example blocked finding.

items.title: Compare job status rows by stable identifier
items.finding: The polling view compares rows by array position, so reordered results can update the wrong row.
items.description: Key status updates by the job identifier and handle added or removed jobs without relying on response order.
research: The API already returns a stable job ID.
validation: Test reordered, inserted, and removed jobs.
Verify only changed rows re-render.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example correctness finding.

items.title: Return a lightweight payload for job status polling
items.finding: The polling endpoint returns complete job records even though the view needs only identity and status fields.
items.description: Add a compact status response and preserve the full-detail endpoint for explicit navigation.
research: Payload size grows with result history and attachments.
validation: Compare response size and database query shape before and after.
Verify polling behavior remains unchanged.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example performance finding.

items.title: Define a consistent health-check failure response
items.finding: A dependency failure sometimes returns success with an error-shaped body and sometimes returns a server error.
items.description: Choose one documented status and response contract for dependency failures and apply it consistently.
research: The deployment monitor's expected failure contract needs confirmation.
validation: Test healthy, degraded, timeout, and dependency-error cases.
Verify the deployment monitor recognizes the selected contract.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example blocked finding.

items.title: Preserve original errors at the repository boundary
items.finding: The repository converts database failures to empty results and discards the original cause.
items.description: Return successful empty results only for valid empty queries and preserve database failures with contextual error information.
research: Current callers cannot distinguish no data from a failed query.
validation: Test empty results separately from database failures.
Verify logs include the original cause and request correlation ID.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example reliability finding.

items.title: Centralize API error responses and correlation IDs
items.finding: Routes translate errors independently, producing inconsistent response bodies and missing correlation IDs.
items.description: Add one error boundary that maps known errors to stable problem responses and logs unexpected failures once.
research: Repository failures must preserve their causes before central handling can add useful context.
validation: Verify validation, authorization, not-found, and unexpected errors use the documented shape.
Confirm every unexpected response includes a correlation ID.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example reliability finding.

items.title: Add separate liveness and readiness endpoints
items.finding: The service has no application-level signal that separates process health from dependency readiness.
items.description: Expose a cheap liveness check and a bounded readiness check for required dependencies.
research: The hosting platform can probe distinct endpoints.
validation: Verify liveness remains available during a dependency outage.
Verify readiness reports unavailable when a required dependency fails.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example operations finding.

items.title: Run a smoke check after deployment
items.finding: The delivery pipeline finishes after process startup without checking application readiness.
items.description: Poll the readiness endpoint with a bounded timeout and fail the deployment when the new version does not become ready.
research: The readiness endpoint should land first so the smoke check has a stable contract.
validation: Verify a healthy deployment passes.
Verify startup failure, timeout, and dependency failure stop the pipeline.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example delivery finding.

items.title: Run server tests in continuous integration
items.finding: The primary validation job builds the server but does not execute its test suite.
items.description: Add the existing server test command to the required validation job and publish test results on failure.
research: The test command is already deterministic on supported runtimes.
validation: Introduce a temporary failing test and confirm the job blocks.
Verify test results are visible in the CI summary.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example testing finding.

items.title: Run client tests in continuous integration
items.finding: Client unit tests are available locally but are omitted from the required validation job.
items.description: Install from the lockfile and run client tests in the same supported runtime used for the production build.
research: The current build step already restores client dependencies.
validation: Confirm a client test failure blocks validation.
Verify the lockfile-only install succeeds in CI.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example testing finding.

items.title: Add integration tests for private download authorization
items.finding: Middleware order and direct download authorization lack integration coverage.
items.description: Exercise anonymous, unrelated-user, and authorized-owner requests through the complete server pipeline.
research: The download fix defines the contract that these tests should lock down.
validation: Verify anonymous requests receive 401 and unrelated users receive 403.
Verify the owner receives the expected file and content type.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example testing finding.

items.title: Add browser coverage for downloads and job polling
items.finding: Two critical user flows have no browser-level regression coverage.
items.description: Cover authorized downloads and stable job polling after their server and client contracts are corrected.
research: The browser scenarios depend on the download and polling fixes.
validation: Run the scenarios against a fresh isolated database.
Verify reordered polling responses and denied downloads are observable in the UI.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example testing finding.

items.title: Profile high-volume database queries before optimizing
items.finding: Several frequently used queries may be slow, but production impact has not been measured.
items.description: Capture duration, row counts, query plans, and concurrent request behavior, then optimize only confirmed hotspots.
research: Representative production-like data volume is still needed.
validation: Record before-and-after query plans for confirmed hotspots.
Run concurrency tests with cancellation enabled.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example investigation finding.

items.title: Use the shared HTTP client for outbound requests
items.finding: One integration creates ad hoc clients and implements timeout and error handling differently from the rest of the service.
items.description: Route the integration through the existing shared client with bounded timeout, cancellation, and consistent error mapping.
research: A shared client is already configured for the other outbound integration.
validation: Test success, non-success status, timeout, cancellation, and malformed responses.
Verify connection reuse under repeated requests.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example reliability finding.

items.title: Move expensive report rendering out of the request path
items.finding: Large reports are rendered synchronously before the request can respond.
items.description: Queue report generation, return a job identifier, and let the existing status flow expose completion.
research: The job infrastructure already supports bounded background work.
validation: Verify requests return promptly for large reports.
Verify failed jobs expose an actionable error without losing diagnostics.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example performance finding.

items.title: Disable development middleware in production
items.finding: Development diagnostics and source serving are enabled without checking the runtime environment.
items.description: Enable development-only middleware explicitly and keep the production pipeline limited to built assets and stable error responses.
research: The environment flag is available during server startup.
validation: Verify development retains diagnostics and live reload.
Verify production does not expose source files or diagnostic pages.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example configuration finding.

items.title: Verify session continuity across service restarts
items.finding: Session behavior after a process restart has not been verified with the deployed storage configuration.
items.description: Test active sessions before and after a restart before introducing additional session infrastructure.
research: The production topology and acceptable reauthentication behavior need owner confirmation.
validation: Test navigation and authenticated API requests across a restart.
Review session and token-acquisition logs for unexpected failures.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example blocked finding.

items.title: Route controller data access through the existing repository
items.finding: One route queries the database client directly and bypasses established repository behavior.
items.description: Add only the missing methods to the existing repository and preserve the route's response contract.
research: The repository already owns logging, filtering, and transaction conventions for this entity.
validation: Verify the route no longer imports the database client.
Preserve response status, shape, ordering, and error behavior.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example architecture finding.

items.title: Consolidate duplicate object-storage helpers
items.finding: Upload and download helpers are duplicated across two server modules and differ in validation and retry behavior.
items.description: Choose the established storage module as owner and migrate one representative caller before removing duplication.
research: Caller-specific authorization must remain at the route boundary.
validation: Compare path validation, retries, and error mapping before migration.
Migrate one caller and verify behavior parity.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example architecture finding.

items.title: Pin supported runtime versions
items.finding: Local and CI environments can resolve different major runtime versions.
items.description: Declare the supported runtime and package-manager versions and align CI with those declarations.
research: The current lockfile was generated with the documented supported versions.
validation: Verify local version resolution matches CI.
Install from the lockfile and run the build on the pinned runtime.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example tooling finding.

items.title: Remove stale deployment instructions
items.finding: Several setup documents describe a retired deployment path and obsolete commands.
items.description: Delete obsolete instructions and keep one supported deployment guide linked from the project readme.
research: The active delivery pipeline defines the supported command sequence.
validation: Search documentation for retired commands and paths.
Follow the supported guide from a clean checkout.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example documentation finding.

items.title: Document the authoritative verification commands
items.finding: Contributors must infer the required validation sequence from CI configuration.
items.description: Document formatting, type, unit, integration, browser, build, and migration checks in one maintained location.
research: The commands exist but ownership and update expectations should be stated.
validation: Run every documented command from a clean checkout.
Verify the readme links to the maintained verification guide.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example documentation finding.

items.title: Add dependency telemetry for critical integrations
items.finding: Database, storage, and outbound HTTP calls do not emit consistent duration and outcome metrics.
items.description: Add structured dependency spans with bounded names, duration, outcome, and correlation while excluding credentials and payloads.
research: Error propagation and centralized handling should be consistent before telemetry is standardized.
validation: Verify success, timeout, cancellation, and error outcomes are distinguishable.
Inspect telemetry for sensitive or high-cardinality fields.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example observability finding.

items.title: Audit third-party dependencies and update policy
items.finding: The project lacks a current inventory and policy for vulnerable or unsupported dependencies.
items.description: Inventory direct dependencies, classify security and support risk, and prepare focused upgrades without bundling unrelated framework changes.
research: Runtime-loaded assets and native packages require separate ownership review.
validation: Run package audits and inspect resolved dependency graphs.
Document accepted exceptions with owners and review dates.

statusProvenance.note: Imported as an example dependency finding.
